messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: error-rate spike on /v2/prompt-proxy-canary (region: us-west). Canary failure threshold breached (5xx > 8% over 5m). Auto-page to oncall.

sarah.oncall: Just saw the page. Looking at traces and the canary dashboard now. Can anyone confirm if this is traffic-related or code regression?

devon.eng: I started a quick grep on the canary logs — lots of 502s hitting new proxy route /rpc/promptv4-proxy (upstream: prompt-router-v2-alpha). Latency also increasing. Nothing obvious in infra scaling.

mike.sre: Checking infra: hosts look healthy, CPU/GPU util normal. Network p95 for the host group spiked slightly but not enough to explain 5xx. Could be upstream model process oom or new route config mismatch.

sarah.oncall: If this is the new proxy path for the experimental prompt routing, we should flip the route flag back to stable. We have emergency revert policy in place.

leo.product: Agree — this is the promptv4 weighted route rollout we started at 09:22. Customer-facing canaries at 5% already. Product wants minimal user impact. Can support draft a message?

anya.support: Support sees a handful of chats from customers complaining about partial responses and retries. No major outage alerts from CS yet, but ticket volume rising. Recommend immediate mitigation.

devon.eng: I'm going to request an emergency feature-flag stomp for the route. Who can apply? I can do it but prefer an SRE double-check before we flip.

mike.sre: I'll be the verifier. sarah, can you page the flag team or run the ff CLI?

sarah.oncall: On it. Executing emergency flag rollback command now.

sarah.oncall (action):
```
# using internal flagctl
flagctl set --env prod --flag promptv4-routing --value stable --reason "emergency stomp: canary 5xx spike"
```

deploy-bot: Flag change recorded: promptv4-routing -> stable by sarah.oncall at 2076543330. Propagation should reach edge routers within ~30s.

devon.eng: Confirmed I see the change in the feature-flag service stream. Starting to observe weight move off the alpha pool.

mike.sre: Tailing logs: 502s sharply drop within 40s. Error-rate back under threshold. p95 latency falling toward baseline.

anya.support: Notifying affected customers with a brief update. Draft: "We've rolled back an experimental routing change that caused intermittent partial responses. We're monitoring and will follow up with details." Want approval?

leo.product: Approve. Keep it short and empathic. Add a note that we will follow up with root cause.

anya.support (sent): Customer message queued and sent to impacted sessions. No blocking escalations so far.

sarah.oncall: handing off to devon.eng for follow-up and RCA. I'm going offline in ~30m; devon, you'll take lead.

devon.eng: Acknowledged, taking lead. Next steps: collect core dumps, reproduce failure in canary, run a targeted config diff between alpha route and stable. I'll also pin model variant logs to see if a model process crashed.

mike.sre: I'll reserve extra logging retention and snapshot the host disks for deeper analysis. Also add a temporary throttling guard on the proxy pool to avoid noisy retries while we investigate.

leo.product: Any idea if we should pause further canaries for this entire release until RCA? I recommend a hold.

devon.eng: Hold agreed. I'll open a deployment hold ticket and tag the release.

incident-bot: Paging escalation: oncall handover recorded — sarah.oncall -> devon.eng at 2076543450.

anya.support: Creating an internal incident summary for customer-facing comms. Will sync with devon and leo before sending a post-incident note.

sarah.oncall: quick note for postmortem: include the rollout weight config, any probe timeout differences, and the flag propagation timing. Also let's add a playbook step to verify model process health during canaries.

devon.eng: Agreed. Early hypothesis: new proxy route had a slightly stricter downstream timeout (200ms) and when model cold-starts overlapped with bursty traffic we saw partial responses bubble up as 502. Will validate.

mike.sre: If that stands, mitigation options: increase timeout, add retry with jitter for alpha pool, and improve pre-warmed model instances for canary traffic.

leo.product: I'll draft the postmortem outline and coordinate with eng for timeline & remediate owners. Let's include action owners and ETA for fixes.

devon.eng: Logging runbook command I used to repro the 502 locally (for handover):
```
# repro with canary weight and synthetic load
loadtest --route /rpc/promptv4-proxy --qps 50 --duration 60s --header "x-canary: true"
```

anya.support: Thanks. I'll add the support ticket IDs to the incident doc.

mike.sre: Left a note to keep the flag in 'stable' until we have a confirmed fix. We'll schedule a canary-only smoke in staging once fixed.

devon.eng: Closing the live mitigation portion. Monitoring for residual errors for another 30m. Will update incident thread with RCA timeline.

leo.product: Thanks everyone. Good coordination. Follow-up: postmortem draft due EOD tomorrow, owners assigned in doc.

incident-bot: Incident resolved for alert group prompt-proxy-canary — severity reduced to S2 at 2076543720.

devon.eng: Final status: 5xx rate normalized, rollback confirmed, customer messages dispatched, hold placed on release. Switching to RCA work.

sarah.oncall: Thanks team — nice quick stomp and recovery.

(reacts: :white_check_mark: from leo.product, :thumbsup: from anya.support)
